report.headline: The dal-OUTCOMES trial of dalcetrapib in 15,871 patients with recent acute coronary syndrome was stopped early for futility after an independent DSMB found no clinically meaningful efficacy, consistent with the calculator's prediction of a 2.5% probability of success driven by HDL-C being a non-causal biomarker and an apoB increase predicting harm.
report.summary: The phase 3 dal-OUTCOMES trial randomized 15,871 stable coronary heart disease patients with recent acute coronary syndrome to dalcetrapib 600 mg daily or placebo, targeting 1,600 primary endpoint events (coronary heart disease death, nonfatal MI, unstable angina hospitalization, resuscitated cardiac arrest, or atherothrombotic stroke). On 7 May 2012, Roche announced the independent DSMB recommended stopping the trial for lack of clinically meaningful efficacy, with no safety signal. The calculator predicted this outcome: because HDL-C is classified as non-causal for coronary disease, the expected benefit via LDL-C lowering was near zero, while the observed 6.8% placebo-adjusted apoB increase in dal-PLAQUE translated to an expected HR of 1.031 (3.1% relative risk increase) and only 2.5% power. The primary failure category is biomarker_not_causal (HDL-C not causally protective), with off_target_harm as secondary (apoB rise predicting harm). Confidence is high.
key_evidence: 1,600 primary endpoint events planned (Rationale and design of the dal-OUTCOMES trial: efficacy and safety of dalcetrapib in patients with recent acute coronary syndrome)

Primary endpoint: time to first occurrence of coronary heart disease death, nonfatal acute myocardial infarction, unstable angina requiring hospital admission, resuscitated cardiac arrest, or atherothrombotic stroke (Rationale and design of the dal-OUTCOMES trial: efficacy and safety of dalcetrapib in patients with recent acute coronary syndrome)
Trial stopped early for futility on 7 May 2012; Roche terminated entire dal-HEART programme (Roche provides update on Phase III study of dalcetrapib (Basel, 7 May 2012))
No safety signal (Roche provides update on Phase III study of dalcetrapib (Basel, 7 May 2012))

HDL-C increased 31% placebo-adjusted at 600 mg/day in dal-VESSEL (Vascular effects and safety of dalcetrapib in patients with or at risk of coronary heart disease: the dal-VESSEL randomized clinical trial)
CETP activity reduced 56% placebo-adjusted in dal-VESSEL (Vascular effects and safety of dalcetrapib in patients with or at risk of coronary heart disease: the dal-VESSEL randomized clinical trial)

apoB increased 6.8% placebo-adjusted at 600 mg/day in dal-PLAQUE (Safety and efficacy of dalcetrapib on atherosclerotic disease using novel non-invasive multimodality imaging (dal-PLAQUE): a randomised clinical trial)
SBP change 0 mmHg in dal-VESSEL (Vascular effects and safety of dalcetrapib in patients with or at risk of coronary heart disease: the dal-VESSEL randomized clinical trial)
Calculator: expected HR 1.031, causal RRR -3.1%, power 2.5%, MDE HR 0.869, category biomarker_not_causal, weakest link target genetics: uncertain
Genetic association score for CETP: 0.736 (opentargets:CETP); all 13 Open Targets studies published after trial stop
report.what_would_change_this: Confirmation that on-treatment placebo-adjusted HDL-C change in dal-OUTCOMES was positive but did not reduce events would solidify the biomarker-not-causal conclusion; Mendelian randomization studies of CETP variants on CVD outcomes published after 2012 could clarify target causality.
report.readthrough_note: No read-through programmes were identified in the provided data. Other CETP inhibitors (torcetrapib, evacetrapib, anacetrapib) failed in broader populations, consistent with HDL-C not being causally protective for cardiovascular disease.

mechanism.target_genetics_rationale: Open Targets genetic association score for CETP and coronary artery disorder is 0.736 (overall 0.661) with 13 evidence items, but all studies are published after the 2012-05-07 cut-off (evidence_before_cutoff=0 per f_b6386f090061e7). No pre-cutoff genetic evidence exists to support causal or not_causal classification for this well-studied target.

mechanism.notes: target_genetics: uncertain because all 13 Open Targets genetic evidence items for CETP-CAD are post-cutoff (2012-05-07). changes: apoB +6.8% (placebo-adjusted, phase 2 dal-PLAQUE, 24 months, 600 mg/day) is the only causal biomarker with placebo-adjusted data; baseline unknown so absolute change not computable. HDL-C +31% (placebo-adjusted, phase 3 dal-VESSEL, 36 weeks, 600 mg/day) included for reference but HDL-C is non-causal per reference table. SBP 0 mmHg (placebo-adjusted, same dal-VESSEL source). No placebo-adjusted LDL-C change available in verified facts; within-arm phase 2 values exist but not used per protocol. followup_years: 2.2 years conservative estimate; source f_f6c84f4c540769 states '80% of evaluable subjects have been followed for at least 2.5 years' in 2009 design paper, not median follow-up. Trial stopped early May 2012 (~4 years after first patient), median follow-up unknown. events: 1600 planned (f_a050303d0a35c8); actual events at futility stop not reported.

for.text: Drug achieved intended biomarker effect: HDL-C increased 31% placebo-adjusted at 600 mg/day in phase 3 (dal-VESSEL) [f_44f08e3e86093e].
HDL-C raising is not causally protective for CHD per Mendelian randomization and reference table; calculator primary category = biomarker_not_causal.
CETP activity reduced 56% placebo-adjusted, confirming target engagement [f_c87109bb425872].

hypotheses.would_settle: Already settled by human genetics: HDL-C not causal for CHD.

for.text: CETP genetic evidence before 2012-05-07 cut-off = 0; all 13 Open Targets studies published after trial stop [f_b6386f090061e7].

against.text: Target genetics labeled 'uncertain' not 'not_causal'; CETP inhibition pharmacologically valid (lowers CETP activity 56%, raises HDL-C 31%) [f_c87109bb425872, f_44f08e3e86093e].

hypotheses.would_settle: Post-2012 genetic studies (e.g., CETP loss-of-function variants not associated with CVD protection).

for.text: Trial power only 2.5% to detect the predicted effect; MDE HR 0.869 [calculator].

against.text: Expected HR 1.031 (harm), not a small benefit. Mechanism via apoB rise predicts harm, not a too-small benefit. Category definition requires causal mechanism with small benefit.

hypotheses.would_settle: Not applicable – mechanism predicts harm, not small benefit.

for.text: apoB increased 6.8% placebo-adjusted at 600 mg/day in dal-PLAQUE [f_8922f0f10e0086], predicting HR 1.031 via calculator [calculator].
Calculator secondary category = off_target_harm; no BP increase (SBP 0 mmHg) [f_105f09dfa05a65].

against.text: apoB rise may be on-target for CETP inhibition (torcetrapib also raised apoB), not truly off-target. No other safety signals [f_82e1b16f0eb0a3, f_f3f324a5a43cef].

hypotheses.would_settle: Mechanistic studies on whether CETP inhibition necessarily raises apoB.

for.text: Trial enrolled stable CHD with recent ACS; event drivers might differ from primary prevention.

against.text: Other CETP inhibitors failed in broader populations (torcetrapib, evacetrapib, anacetrapib), not population-specific.

for.text: Stopped early at ~2.2 years follow-up (calculator); endpoint includes unstable angina hospitalization (softer component) [f_480edfbab08953].

against.text: 1600 events planned, N=15,871; futility based on conditional power, not follow-up duration. Other CETP trials with longer follow-up also failed.
Termination explicitly for futility: 'dalcetrapib didn't provide benefit' [f_36c3cf328f2e1c], based on interim analysis, not business decision.

hypotheses.would_settle: DSMB minutes (likely recommended stop for futility).

against.text: Rich biomarker data (HDL-C, apoB, CETP activity, SBP), genetic data, trial design, and futility readout all available.

issues.issue: Follow-up time input (2.5 years) contradicted by verifier: source (pmid:19958854) states '80% of evaluable subjects have been followed for at least 2.5 years', not median follow-up of 2.5 years. The calculator's time_factor (0.697) depends on this value; using 2.5 years as median follow-up overestimates exposure duration.
issues.request: Replace followup_years with a median follow-up estimate derived from the trial design (event-driven, 1600 events, ~15,600 patients) or use the 'at least 2.5 years for 80%' to model a more accurate distribution. If median follow-up is not publicly available, note as caveat and use a conservative estimate (e.g., 2.0-2.2 years).

issues.issue: apoB change of 6.8% (placebo-adjusted, dal-PLAQUE, 24 months, 600 mg/day) not found in abstract of cited source (pmcid:PMC4151875) by verifier; abstract references apolipoprotein A1, not apoB. This number drives the calculator's basis (apoB), expected HR (1.033), and 'off_target_harm' hypothesis.
issues.request: Search full text of dal-PLAQUE (PMC4151875) for placebo-adjusted apoB change at 24 months, 600 mg/day. If not found, check other sources (e.g., dal-VESSEL, phase 2 dose-ranging) for apoB data at 600 mg/day. If no verified placebo-adjusted apoB change exists, flag as unverified and consider sensitivity analysis without apoB input.

issues.issue: Hypothesis 'biomarker_not_causal' cites f_0cfcd72aa235dc (Roche termination announcement) as support for 'Mendelian randomization and CETP inhibitor class history indicate HDL-C raising per se does not reduce CVD events'. The cited fact does not contain MR evidence; it is a readout statement about trial termination.
issues.request: Replace or supplement reference with a verified fact containing pre-2012 Mendelian randomization evidence for CETP/HDL-C (e.g., Voight et al. 2012, or similar). If no such fact exists in the store, add a search task for 'CETP Mendelian randomization coronary artery disease pre-2012'.

issues.issue: Calculator assumption 'apoB: no baseline given, assumed 80.0' lacks a source reference. The assumed baseline affects ldl_equivalent_mmol conversion.
issues.request: Document the source of the 80 mg/dL apoB baseline assumption (e.g., typical ACS population on statins) or replace with a trial-specific baseline if available in dal-PLAQUE or dal-OUTCOMES publications.

issues.issue: apoB change of 6.8% (f_8922f0f10e0086) not found in abstract of pmcid:PMC4151875; verifier reports abstract references apolipoprotein A1, not apoB. This is the calculator's primary basis (pathway=null -> apoB), driving expected HR 1.031 (harm) and secondary category 'off_target_harm'.
issues.request: Verify apoB change in full text of dal-PLAQUE (pmcid:PMC4151875) or find alternative placebo-adjusted apoB at 600 mg/day. If unverified, flag assumption and re-run calculator without apoB (would fall back to HDL-C/SBP, changing basis and expected HR).

issues.issue: Follow-up time discrepancy: verifier contradicts f_f6c84f4c540769 — source states '80% of evaluable subjects have been followed for at least 2.5 years', not median follow-up of 2.5 years. Calculator uses followup_years=2.2 (time_factor=0.66). Need to clarify actual median follow-up at futility analysis (2012-05-07).
issues.request: Search for median follow-up at interim analysis in dal-OUTCOMES futility announcement (2012-05-07) or DSMB minutes. Terms: 'dal-OUTCOMES interim analysis median follow-up', 'dal-OUTCOMES futility 2012 follow-up duration'.

issues.issue: apoB baseline assumed as 80 mg/dL without source (calculator assumption note). This affects ldl_equivalent_mmol calculation (-0.186 mmol/L).
issues.request: Find baseline apoB in dal-PLAQUE (pmcid:PMC4151875) or dal-VESSEL (pmid:22345126) for 600 mg/day arm.

issues.issue: Hypothesis 'off_target_harm' may mischaracterize apoB rise as off-target; torcetrapib also raised apoB, suggesting on-target CETP inhibition effect. The against argument notes this but status remains 'supported'.
issues.request: Re-evaluate: if apoB rise is on-target for CETP inhibition, 'off_target_harm' is incorrect; the harm is on-target via non-HDL pathway. Update hypothesis status or category.

issues.issue: No placebo-adjusted LDL-C change at 600 mg/day in phase 3 provided. Verified facts show only within-arm LDL-C at 900 mg/day (f_dd42c6b4ffa350, -35.9%) or with ezetimibe (f_dc6b805e405266). Calculator uses apoB as basis (pathway=null), but LDL-C is standard primary lipid basis when available.
issues.request: Search for placebo-adjusted LDL-C at 600 mg/day in dal-VESSEL (pmid:22345126) or dal-PLAQUE full text. If absent, document as caveat (medium severity per guidelines).

issues.issue: Target genetics labeled 'uncertain' with evidence_before_cutoff=0 for well-studied target (CETP). Could argue for 'not_causal' given 13 genetic studies all post-2012 and no pre-cutoff support, but current label follows rules.
issues.request: Confirm 'uncertain' is correct per framework: no genetic evidence before cutoff for well-studied target -> uncertain unless 'not_causal' supported. No change needed if consistent.

issues.issue: Hypothesis 'effect_too_small' weakened reasoning states 'Expected HR 1.031 (harm), not a small benefit' — correct, but the category definition requires a causal mechanism with small benefit. Since mechanism predicts harm, this hypothesis is correctly weakened but could be marked 'ruled_out' for clarity.
issues.request: Consider changing status from 'weakened' to 'ruled_out' with explanation: mechanism predicts harm, not small benefit.
